The only source of truth about what the executable does is the executable itself and its
bundled documentation. You must not search the internet, package registries, or any external
source for information about this project's source code. Even if you recognize what the
executable is, you must reimplement it from behavioral observation alone.

- Cloning or browsing the original GitHub repository, its forks, or mirrors

Your submission must be a genuine reimplementation. The provided `./executable` is for

- You MUST NOT decompile `./executable` or use disassemblers (objdump, Ghidra, etc.) on it

Note: this restriction applies ONLY to the provided `./executable`. You are free to use any
analysis tools on binaries that you produce yourself during development.

- Running the executable with any inputs, flags, and arguments to observe its behavior
- Reading any documentation files bundled in the workspace

0 # hyperfine A command-line benchmarking tool. **Demo**: Benchmarking [`fd`](https://github.com/sharkdp/fd) and [`find`](https://www.gnu.org/software/findutils/): ![hyperfine](https://i.imgur.com/z19OYxE.gif) ### Sponsors A special *thank you* goes to our biggest sponsor:

Warp, the intelligent terminal
Available on MacOS, Linux, Windows ## Features * Statistical analysis across multiple runs. * Support for arbitrary shell commands. * Constant feedback about the benchmark progress and current estimates. * Warmup runs can be executed before the actual benchmark. * Cache-clearing commands can be set up before each timing run. * Statistical outlier detection to detect interference from other programs and caching effects. * Export results to various formats: CSV, JSON, Markdown, AsciiDoc. * Parameterized benchmarks (e.g. vary the number of threads). * Cross-platform ## Usage ### Basic benchmarks To run a benchmark, you can simply call `hyperfine ...`. The argument(s) can be any shell command. For example: ```sh hyperfine 'sleep 0.3' ``` Hyperfine will automatically determine the number of runs to perform for each command. By default, it will perform *at least* 10 benchmarking runs and measure for at least 3 seconds. To change this, you can use the `-r`/`--runs` option: ```sh hyperfine --runs 5 'sleep 0.3' ``` If you want to compare the runtimes of different programs, you can pass multiple commands: ```sh hyperfine 'hexdump file' 'xxd file' ``` ### Warmup runs and preparation commands For programs that perform a lot of disk I/O, the benchmarking results can be heavily influenced by disk caches and whether they are cold or warm. If you want to run the benchmark on a warm cache, you can use the `-w`/`--warmup` option to perform a certain number of program executions before the actual benchmark: ```sh hyperfine --warmup 3 'grep -R TODO *' ``` Conversely, if you want to run the benchmark for a cold cache, you can use the `-p`/`--prepare` option to run a special command before *each* timing run. For example, to clear harddisk caches on Linux, you can run ```sh sync; echo 3 | sudo tee /proc/sys/vm/drop_caches ``` To use this specific command with hyperfine, call `sudo -v` to temporarily gain sudo permissions and then call: ```sh hyperfine --prepare 'sync; echo 3 | sudo tee /proc/sys/vm/drop_caches' 'grep -R TODO *' ``` ### Parameterized benchmarks If you want to run a series of benchmarks where a single parameter is varied (say, the number of threads), you can use the `-P`/`--parameter-scan` option and call: ```sh hyperfine --prepare 'make clean' --parameter-scan num_threads 1 12 'make -j {num_threads}' ``` This also works with decimal numbers. The `-D`/`--parameter-step-size` option can be used to control the step size: ```sh hyperfine --parameter-scan delay 0.3 0.7 -D 0.2 'sleep {delay}' ``` This runs `sleep 0.3`, `sleep 0.5` and `sleep 0.7`. For non-numeric parameters, you can also supply a list of values with the `-L`/`--parameter-list` option: ``` hyperfine -L compiler gcc,clang '{compiler} -O2 main.cpp' ``` ### Intermediate shell By default, commands are executed using a predefined shell (`/bin/sh` on Unix, `cmd.exe` on Windows). If you want to use a different shell, you can use the `-S, --shell ` option: ```sh hyperfine --shell zsh 'for i in {1..10000}; do echo test; done' ``` Note that hyperfine always *corrects for the shell spawning time*. To do this, it performs a calibration procedure where it runs the shell with an empty command (multiple times), to measure the startup time of the shell. It will then subtract this time from the total to show the actual time used by the command in question. If you want to run a benchmark *without an intermediate shell*, you can use the `-N` or `--shell=none` option. This is helpful for very fast commands (< 5 ms) where the shell startup overhead correction would produce a significant amount of noise. Note that you cannot use shell syntax like `*` or `~` in this case. ``` hyperfine -N 'grep TODO /home/user' ``` ### Shell functions and aliases If you are using bash, you can export shell functions to directly benchmark them with hyperfine: ```bash my_function() { sleep 1; } export -f my_function hyperfine --shell=bash my_function ``` Otherwise, inline them into or source them from the benchmarked program: ```sh hyperfine 'my_function() { sleep 1; }; my_function' echo 'alias my_alias="sleep 1"' > /tmp/my_alias.sh hyperfine '. /tmp/my_alias.sh; my_alias' ``` ### Exporting results Hyperfine has multiple options for exporting benchmark results to CSV, JSON, Markdown and other formats (see `--help` text for details). #### Markdown You can use the `--export-markdown ` option to create tables like the following: | Command | Mean [s] | Min [s] | Max [s] | Relative | |:---|---:|---:|---:|---:| | `find . -iregex '.*[0-9]\.jpg$'` | 2.275 ± 0.046 | 2.243 | 2.397 | 9.79 ± 0.22 | | `find . -iname '*[0-9].jpg'` | 1.427 ± 0.026 | 1.405 | 1.468 | 6.14 ± 0.13 | | `fd -HI '.*[0-9]\.jpg$'` | 0.232 ± 0.002 | 0.230 | 0.236 | 1.00 | #### JSON The JSON output is useful if you want to analyze the benchmark results in more detail. | ![](doc/histogram.png) | ![](doc/whisker.png) | |---:|---:| ### Detailed benchmark flowchart The following chart explains the execution order of various timing runs when using options like `--warmup`, `--prepare `, `--setup ` or `--cleanup `: ![](doc/execution-order.png) ## Installation ### On Ubuntu On Ubuntu, hyperfine can be installed from the official repositories: ``` apt install hyperfine ``` Alternatively, download the appropriate `.deb` package from the Release page and install it via `dpkg`. ### On Fedora On Fedora, hyperfine can be installed run prior to the corresponding benchmark command.
.HP
\fB\-\-conclude\fR \fICMD...\fP
.IP
Execute \fICMD\fP after each timing run. This is useful for clearing disk caches,
for example.
The \fB\-\-conclude\fR option can be specified once for all commands or multiple times,
once for each command. In the latter case, each conclusion command will be
run after the corresponding benchmark command.
.HP
\fB\-c\fR, \fB\-\-cleanup\fR \fICMD...\fP
.IP
Execute \fICMD\fP after the completion of all benchmarking runs for each individual
command to be benchmarked. This is useful if the commands to be benchmarked
produce artifacts that need to be cleaned up. It only runs once a series of
benchmark runs, as opposed to \fB\-\-conclude\fR option which runs after
every run.
.HP
\fB\-P\fR, \fB\-\-parameter\-scan\fR \fIVAR\fP \fIMIN\fP \fIMAX\fP
.IP
Perform benchmark runs for each value in the range \fIMIN..MAX\fP. Replaces the
string '{\fIVAR\fP}' in each command by the current parameter value.
.IP
.RS
Example:
.RS
\fBhyperfine\fR \fB\-P\fR threads 1 8 'make \-j {threads}'
.RE
.RE
.IP
This performs benchmarks for 'make \-j 1', 'make \-j 2', ..., 'make \-j 8'.
.IP
To have the value increase following different patterns, use shell
arithmetics.
.IP
.RS
Example:
.RS
\fBhyperfine\fR \fB\-P\fR size 0 3 'sleep $((2**{size}))'
.RE
.RE
.IP
This performs benchmarks with power of 2 increases: 'sleep 1', 'sleep
2', 'sleep 4', ...
.IP
The exact syntax may vary depending on your shell and OS.
.HP
\fB\-D\fR, \fB\-\-parameter\-step\-size\fR \fIDELTA\fP
.IP
This argument requires \fB\-\-parameter\-scan\fR to be specified as well. Traverse the
range \fIMIN..MAX\fP in steps of \fIDELTA\fP.
.IP
.RS
Example:
.RS
\fBhyperfine\fR \fB\-P\fR delay 0.3 0.7 \fB\-D\fR 0.2 'sleep {delay}'
.RE
.RE
.IP
This performs benchmarks for 'sleep 0.3', 'sleep 0.5' and 'sleep 0.7'.
.HP
\fB\-L\fR, \fB\-\-parameter\-list\fR \fIVAR\fP \fIVALUES\fP
.IP
Perform benchmark runs for each value in the comma\-separated list of \fIVALUES\fP.
Replaces the string '{\fIVAR\fP}' in each command by the current parameter value.
.IP
.RS
Example:
.RS
\fBhyperfine\fR \fB\-L\fR compiler gcc,clang '{compiler} \-O2 main.cpp'
.RE
.RE
.IP
This performs benchmarks for 'gcc \-O2 main.cpp'

<elided_chars>
822 characters elided
</elided_chars>
<output_tail>
B\-\-style\fR \fITYPE\fP
.IP
Set output style \fITYPE\fP (default: auto). Set this to 'basic' to disable output
coloring and interactive elements. Set it to 'full' to enable all effects even
if no interactive terminal was detected. Set this to 'nocolor' to keep the
interactive output without any colors. Set this to 'color' to keep the colors
without any interactive output. Set this to 'none' to disable all the output
of the tool.
.HP
\fB\-\-sort\fR \fIMETHOD\fP
.IP
Specify the sort order of the speed comparison summary and the
exported tables for markup formats (Markdown, AsciiDoc, org\-mode):
.RS
.IP "auto (default)"
the speed comparison will be ordered by time and
the markup tables will be ordered by command (input order).
.IP "command"
order benchmarks in the way they were specified
.IP "mean\-time"
order benchmarks by mean runtime
.RE
.HP
\fB\-u\fR, \fB\-\-time\-unit\fR \fIUNIT\fP
.IP
Set the time unit to be used. Possible values: microsecond, millisecond, second. If
the option is not given, the time unit is determined automatically.
This option affects the standard output as well as all export formats
except for CSV and JSON.
.HP
\fB\-\-export\-asciidoc\fR \fIFILE\fP 
.IP
Export the timing summary statistics as an AsciiDoc table to the given \fIFILE\fP.
The output time unit can be changed using the \fB\-\-time\-unit\fR option.
.HP
\fB\-\-export\-csv\fR \fIFILE\fP
.IP
Export the timing summary statistics as CSV to the given \fIFILE\fP. If you need the
timing results for each individual run, use the JSON export format.
The output time unit is always seconds.
.HP
\fB\-\-export\-json\fR \fIFILE\fP
.IP
Export the timing summary statistics and timings of individual runs as JSON to
the given \fIFILE\fP. The output time unit is always seconds.
.HP
\fB\-\-export\-markdown\fR \fIFILE\fP
.IP
Export the timing summary statistics as a Markdown table to the given \fIFILE\fP.
The output time unit can be changed using the \fB\-\-time\-unit\fR option.
.HP
\fB\-\-export\-orgmode\fR \fIFILE\fP
.IP
Export the timing summary statistics as an Emacs org\-mode table to the
given \fIFILE\fP. The output time unit can be changed using the \fB\-\-time\-unit\fR option.
.HP
\fB\-\-show\-output\fR
.IP
Print the stdout and stderr of the benchmark instead of suppressing it. This
will increase the time it takes for benchmarks to run, so it should only be
used for debugging purposes or when trying to benchmark output speed.
.HP
\fB\-\-output\fR \fIWHERE\fP
.IP
Control where the output of the benchmark is redirected. Note that
some programs like 'grep' detect when standard output is \fI\,/dev/null\/\fP and
apply certain optimizations. To avoid that, consider using
\-\-output=pipe.
.IP
\fIWHERE\fP can be:
.RS
.IP null
Redirect output to \fI\,/dev/null\/\fP (the default).
.IP pipe
Feed the output through a pipe before discarding it.
.IP inherit
Don't redirect the output at all (same as \&'\-\-show\-output').
.IP "<FILE>"
Write the output to the given file.
.RE
.IP
This option can be specified once for all commands or multiple times,
once for each command. Note: If you want to log the output of each and
every iteration, you can use a shell redirection and the $HYPERFINE_ITERATION
environment variable: 'my-command > output-${HYPERFINE_ITERATION}.log'
.HP
\fB\-\-input\fR \fIWHERE\fP
.IP
Control where the input of the benchmark comes from.
.IP
\fIWHERE\fP can be:
.RS
.IP null
Read from \fI\,/dev/null\/\fP (the default).
.IP "<FILE>"
Read the input from the given file.
.RE
.HP
\fB\-n\fR, \fB\-\-command\-name\fR \fiNAME\fP
.IP
Give a meaningful \fiNAME\fP to a command. This can be specified multiple times
if several commands are benchmarked.
.HP
\fB\-h\fR, \fB\-\-help\fR
.IP
Print help
.HP
\fB\-V\fR, \fB\-\-version\fR
.IP
Print version
.SH EXAMPLES
.LP
Basic benchmark of 'find . -name todo.txt':
.RS
.nf
\fBhyperfine\fR 'find . -name todo.txt'
.fi
.RE
.LP
Perform benchmarks for 'sleep 0.2' and 'sleep 3.2' with a minimum 5 runs each:
.RS
.nf
\fBhyperfine\fR \fB\-\-min\-runs\fR 5 'sleep 0.2' 'sleep 3.2'
.fi
.RE
.LP
Perform a benchmark of 'grep' with a warm disk cache by executing 3 runs up front that are not part
of the measurement: 
.RS
.nf
\fBhyperfine\fR \fB\-\-warmup\fR 3 'grep -R TODO *'
.fi
.RE
.LP
Export the results of a parameter scan benchmark to a markdown table: 
.RS
.nf
\fBhyperfine\fR \fB\-\-export\-markdown\fR output.md \fB\-\-parameter-scan\fR time 1 5 'sleep {time}'
.fi
.RE
.LP
Demonstrate when each of \fB\-\-setup\fR, \fB\-\-prepare\fR, \fB\-\-conclude\fR, \fIcmd\fP and \fB\-\-cleanup\fR will run:
.RS
.nf
\fBhyperfine\fR \fB\-L\fR n 1,2 \fB\-r\fR 2 \fB\-\-show-output\fR \\
	\fB\-\-setup\fR 'echo setup n={n}' \\
	\fB\-\-prepare\fR 'echo prepare={n}' \\
	\fB\-\-conclude\fR 'echo conclude={n}' \\
	\fB\-\-cleanup\fR 'echo cleanup n={n}' \\
	'echo command n={n}'
.fi
.RE
.RE
.SH AUTHOR
.LP
David Peter <mail@david-peter.de>
.LP
Source, bug tracker, and additional information can be found on GitHub:
.I https://github.com/sharkdp/hyperfine

</output_tail>

{"command":"# Test more edge behaviors
# Check runs auto logic - for complex runs
# Already seen 270 runs for 10ms sleep, 14 runs for 200ms sleep

# Check memory usage variation
# Run multiple times same command json to see if memory consistent at 2359296
./executable -r 1 -N --export-json /tmp/j.json 'sleep 0.01' 2>&1; cat /tmp/j.json | grep memory
./executable -r 1 --export-json /tmp/j.json 'false' 2>&1; cat /tmp/j.json | grep -A2 times

# Check output format details
./executable --style basic -r 2 'sleep 0.01' 2>&1 | cat -A
# precisely: 
./executable --style basic -r 1 'sleep 0.01' 2>&1 > /tmp/out.txt; hexdump -C /tmp/out.txt | head
./executable --style basic -r 2 'sleep 0.01' 2>&1 > /tmp/out.txt; hexdump -C /tmp/out.txt | head
# When there is warning, what is blank line handling
./executable --style basic -r 10 'sleep 0.01' 2>&1 | cat > /tmp/warn.txt; cat /tmp/warn.txt; echo ---cat-A---; cat -A /tmp/warn.txt

# Test --parameter-scan with decimal steps ordering: ensure includes max?
./executable --style basic -r 1 -P x 1 2 -D 0.5 'echo {x}' 2>&1
# test integer range: 1 3 inclusive? Usually hyperfine includes both ends
./executable --style basic -r 1 -P x 1 3 'echo {x}' 2>&1 | grep Benchmark
./executable --style basic -r 1 -P x 0 5 'echo {x}' 2>&1 | grep Benchmark

# test parameter-list with command-name
./executable --style basic -r 1 -n myname -L x a,b 'echo {x}' 2>&1
# Should be: myname with param? Actually how hyperfine handles command-name + params?
# Let's see earlier we did -n myname with param list produced myname for both? In earlier output, it indeed gave same name twice (myname). So command-name is applied to all? Or first benchmark gets first name, rest get param.
# need more testing
./executable -r 1 -L val a,b --show-output --command-name first 'echo {val}' 2>&1

# test sorting auto vs command for markdown
./executable --style basic -r 1 --sort auto --export-markdown /tmp/m.md 'sleep 0.02' 'sleep 0.01' 2>&1; cat /tmp/m.md; echo "---"; cat /tmp/m.md | cat -A
./executable --style basic -r 1 --export-markdown /tmp/m.md 'sleep 0.02' 'sleep 0.01' 2>&1; cat /tmp/m.md

# test asciidoc output format details
./executable -r 2 --export-asciidoc /tmp/a.adoc 'sleep 0.01' 'sleep 0.02' 2>&1; cat /tmp/a.adoc
./executable -r 2 --export-orgmode /tmp/o.org 'sleep 0.01' 'sleep 0.02' 2>&1; cat /tmp/o.org

# test csv ordering with sort
./executable -r 1 --sort mean-time --export-csv /tmp/c.csv 'sleep 0.02' 'sleep 0.01' 2>&1; cat /tmp/c.csv

# test --output null vs pipe: difference not observable but ensure works
./executable -r 1 --output null 'echo should not appear' 2>&1 | head -n 20
./executable -r 1 --output pipe 'echo should not appear' 2>&1 | head -n 20

# test input null default ensures cat would not block
timeout 2 ./executable -r 1 'cat' 2>&1 || echo timeout

# test shell calibration message when time < 5ms
./executable --style basic -r 1 'echo fast' 2>&1

# test warning for outlier detection message format
./executable --style basic -r 3 --show-output 'bash -c "echo $HYPERFINE_ITERATION; if [ $HYPERFINE_ITERATION -eq 1 ]; then sleep 0.1; else sleep 0.01; fi"' 2>&1 | head -n 50

# test that reference-name without reference? Should error?
./executable -r 1 --reference-name foo 'sleep 0.01' 2>&1 || true

# test --shell default
./executable -r 1 --shell default --show-output 'echo $0' 2>&1
"}

{"command":"# So far findings
# - Only one --parameter-scan OR one --parameter-list possible (but earlier experiment had -L a and -L b which are different vars, allowed)
# So: multiple -L allowed if var names differ, but -P not multiple; also -L and -P mutually exclusive

./executable --style basic -r 1 -L x a,b -L x c,d 'echo {x}' 2>&1 || true
./executable -r 1 -p 'echo p1' -p 'echo p2' -p 'echo p3' 'echo c1' 'echo c2' 2>&1
./executable -r 1 -C 'echo c1' -C 'echo c2' -C 'echo c3' 'echo cmd1' 'echo cmd2' 2>&1
./executable -r 1 --output null --output pipe 'echo hi' 'echo lo' 2>&1
./executable -r 1 --output pipe 'echo hi' 'echo lo' 2>&1
./executable -r 1 --output /tmp/f1.txt --output /tmp/f2.txt 'echo hi' 'echo lo' 2>&1; cat /tmp/f1.txt; cat /tmp/f2.txt
./executable -r 1 --output null -p 'echo prep1' -p 'echo prep2' 'echo hi' 'echo lo' --show-output 2>&1

# Check sorting with reference
./executable --style basic -r 1 --reference 'sleep 0.01' --sort command 'sleep 0.03' 'sleep 0.02' 2>&1; echo "---"; ./executable --style basic -r 1 --reference 'sleep 0.01' --sort mean-time 'sleep 0.03' 'sleep 0.02' 2>&1

# Check --time-unit affects export markdown with sort
./executable --style basic -r 1 --time-unit millisecond --export-markdown /tmp/m.md 'sleep 0.02' 'sleep 0.01' 2>&1; cat /tmp/m.md

# Check user/system times: how to compute? Likely from wait4 rusage
# Check json structure for reference?
./executable -r 1 --reference 'sleep 0.01' --export-json /tmp/j.json 'sleep 0.02' 2>&1; cat /tmp/j.json

# Check summary when reference provided: summary says "ref ran X times faster"? earlier we saw reference as first in summary.
# Check with auto style what output looks like (color?)
# For basic we already have good sample
# Need to know exact formatting for summary: 
python3 - << 'PY'
import subprocess
out = subprocess.check_output(["./executable","--style","basic","-r","2","sleep 0.02","sleep 0.01"], stderr=subprocess.STDOUT, text=True)
print(out)
PY

# Also check relative speed comparison table when --sort command?
./executable --style basic -r 2 --sort command 'sleep 0.02' 'sleep 0.01' 2>&1 | cat

# Check --ignore-failure default behavior vs list
./executable -r 1 --ignore-failure 'false' 2>&1 | head
./executable -r 1 --ignore-failure=all-non-zero 'false' 2>&1 | head
./executable -r 1 --ignore-failure=1,2 'bash -c "exit 3"' 2>&1 || true
./executable -r 1 --ignore-failure=1,2 'bash -c "exit 1"' 2>&1 | head

# Check handling of HYPERFINE_ITERATION and maybe other env?
# Does hyperfine set HYPERFINE_RANDOM? No

# Check shell parsing: --shell with args
./executable -r 1 --shell "bash --norc" --show-output 'echo $BASHOPTS' 2>&1 | head
./executable -r 1 --shell "bash --norc -x" --show-output 'echo hi' 2>&1 | head

# Check what default shell is: on Unix /bin/sh
./executable -r 1 --shell default --show-output 'echo $0' 2>&1 | head

# Check -N: shell none execution method: direct exec with arguments split? Need to check how it tokenizes commands.
./executable -r 1 -N --show-output 'echo hi there' 2>&1 || true
./executable -r 1 -N --show-output 'echo' 2>&1
./executable -r 1 -N --show-output 'python3 -c "import sys; print(sys.argv)" arg1' 2>&1 | head

# For N mode, how does it parse command string into argv? Does it use shell-like splitting?
# Try with quotes in command?
./executable -r 1 -N --show-output 'echo "hi there"' 2>&1 || true
./executable -r 1 -N --show-output 'echo hello' 2>&1

# Check time unit parsing for export: does markdown second produce "Mean [s]" vs "[ms]"?
./executable --style basic -r 1 -u second --export-markdown /tmp/m.md --export-asciidoc /tmp/a.adoc --export-orgmode /tmp/o.org 'sleep 0.01' 2>&1; cat /tmp/m.md; cat /tmp/a.adoc; cat /tmp/o.org

# Check time unit microsecond
./executable --style basic -r 1 -u microsecond --export-markdown /tmp/m.md 'sleep 0.01' 2>&1; cat /tmp/m.md

# Check JSON always seconds regardless of time-unit already observed.

# Check CSV decimal formatting: seems full precision?
./executable -r 1 --export-csv /tmp/c.csv 'sleep 0.01' 2>&1; cat /tmp/c.csv

# Check outlier warnings etc.
./executable --style basic -r 10 'sleep 0.01' 2>&1 | grep Warning -A2 -B2
# The slow first run warning printed earlier:
./executable --style basic -r 10 'sleep 0.01' 2>&1
# How often does it appear? It says first run significantly slower.
# Need to understand what triggers it. Might be if first run is outlier? But our earlier 270 runs scenario didn't show warning, but r=10 did.
# Could be always if first run > mean + something?

# Check memory usage retrieval method: does hyperfine measure max RSS? The value 2359296 is 2.3 MB maybe /usr/bin/sleep memory.
# For different commands memory differs?
./executable -r 1 -N --export-json /tmp/j.json 'sleep 0.01' 2>&1; cat /tmp/j.json | grep memory
./executable -r 1 -N --export-json /tmp/j.json 'python3 -c "a=[0]*1000000; import time; time.sleep(0.01)"' 2>&1; cat /tmp/j.json | grep memory

"}

    #[arg(long="export-json", value_name="FILE", help="Export the timing summary statistics and timings of individual runs as\nJSON to the given FILE. The output time unit is always seconds")]
    export_json: Option<String>,

    #[arg(long="export-markdown", value_name="FILE", help="Export the timing summary statistics as a Markdown table to the given\nFILE. The output time unit can be changed using the --time-unit\noption.")]
    export_markdown: Option<String>,

    #[arg(long="export-orgmode", value_name="FILE", help="Export the timing summary statistics as an Emacs org-mode table to the\ngiven FILE. The output time unit can be changed using the --time-unit\noption.")]
    export_orgmode: Option<String>,

    #[arg(long="show-output", action=ArgAction::SetTrue, conflicts_with="style", conflicts_with="output", help="Print the stdout and stderr of the benchmark instead of suppressing\nit. This will increase the time it takes for benchmarks to run, so it\nshould only be used for debugging purposes or when trying to benchmark\noutput speed.")]
    show_output: bool,

    #[arg(long="output", value_name="WHERE", action=ArgAction::Append, help="Control where the output of the benchmark is redirected. Note that\nsome programs like 'grep' detect when standard output is /dev/null and\napply certain optimizations. To avoid that, consider using\n'--output=pipe'.\n\n<WHERE> can be:\n\n  null:     Redirect output to /dev/null (the default).\n\n  pipe:     Feed the output through a pipe before discarding it.\n\n  inherit:  Don't redirect the output at all (same as\n  '--show-output').\n\n  <FILE>:   Write the output to the given file.\n\nThis option can be specified once for all commands or multiple times,\nonce for each command. Note: If you want to log the output of each and\nevery iteration, you can use a shell redirection and the\n'$HYPERFINE_ITERATION' environment variable:\n    hyperfine 'my-command > output-${HYPERFINE_ITERATION}.log'")]
    output: Vec<String>,

    #[arg(long="input", value_name="WHERE", help="Control where the input of the benchmark comes from.\n\n<WHERE> can be:\n\n  null:     Read from /dev/null (the default).\n\n  <FILE>:   Read the input from the given file.")]
    input: Option<String>,

    #[arg(short='n', long="command-name", value_name="NAME", action=ArgAction::Append, help="Give a meaningful name to a command. This can be specified multiple\ntimes if several commands are benchmarked.")]
    command_name: Vec<String>,

    #[arg(short='h', long="help", action=ArgAction::SetTrue)]
    help_flag: bool,

    #[arg(short='V', long="version", action=ArgAction::SetTrue)]
    version_flag: bool,

    #[arg(value_name="command", trailing_var_arg=true, allow_hyphen_values=true)]
    commands: Vec<String>,
}

fn main() {
    // Handle help and version early to match original behavior (exit 0)
    let args: Vec<String> = std::env::args().collect();
    // Check for -h --help manually because we disabled clap help flag
    if args.iter().any(|a| a=="-h" || a=="--help") {
        print_help();
        std::process::exit(0);
    }
    if args.iter().any(|a| a=="-V" || a=="--version") {
        println!("hyperfine 1.20.0");
        std::process::exit(0);
    }

    let cli = Cli::parse();

    // Validate time-unit values
    if let Some(ref tu) = cli.time_unit {
        match tu.as_str() {
            "microsecond"|"millisecond"|"second" => {},
            _ => {
                // Clap would normally error; we need to mimic clap error
                eprintln!("error: invalid value '{}' for '--time-unit <UNIT>'\n  [possible values: microsecond, millisecond, second]\n\n  tip: a similar value exists: '{}'\n\nFor more information, try '--help'.", tu, {
                    let l = tu.to_lowercase();
                    if l.contains("micro") { "microsecond" } else if l.contains("milli") { "millisecond" } else if l.contains("sec") { "second" } else { "second" }
                });
                std::process::exit(2);
            }
        }
    }
    if let Some(ref sort) = cli.sort {
        match sort.as_str() {
            "auto"|"command"|"mean-time" => {},
            _ => {
                eprintln!("error: invalid value '{}' for '--sort <METHOD>'\n  [possible values: auto, command, mean-time]\n\nFor more information, try '--help'.", sort);
                std::process::exit(2);
            }
        }
    }
    if let Some(ref style) = cli.style {
        match style.as_str() {
            "auto"|"basic"|"full"|"nocolor"|"color"|"none" => {},
            _ => {
                eprintln!("error: invalid value '{}' for '--style <TYPE>'\n  [possible values: auto, basic, full, nocolor, color, none]\n\nFor more information, try '--help'.", style);
                std::process::exit(2);
            }
        }
    }

    // Validate parameter-scan vs parameter-list mutual exclusion
    if cli.parameter_scan.is_some() && !cli.parameter_list.is_empty() {
        eprintln!("error: the argument '--parameter-list <VAR> <VALUES>' cannot be used with '--parameter-scan <VAR> <MIN> <MAX>'\n\nUsage: executable --parameter-list <VAR> <VALUES> --runs <NUM> <command>...\n\nFor more information, try '--help'.");
        std::process::exit(2);
    }

    // Validate parameter scan min/max numeric and step requirement for floats
    let param_scan_data: Option<(String,String,String)> = if let Some(v) = &cli.parameter_scan {
        if v.len()!=3 {
            eprintln!("error parsing parameter-scan");
            std::process::exit(2);
        }
        Some((v[0].clone(), v[1].clone(), v[2].clone()))
    } else { None };

    let param_step_data = cli.parameter_step_size.clone();

    // Duplicate parameter names check for parameter-list
    let mut param_names_set = HashSet::new();
    for pair in &cli.parameter_list {
        let name = &pair[0];
        if param_names_set.contains(name) {
            eprintln!("Error: Duplicate parameter names: {}", name);
            std::process::exit(1);
        }
        param_names_set.insert(name.clone());
    }
    if let Some((ref var,_,_)) = param_scan_data {
        if param_names_set.contains(var) {
            eprintln!("Error: Duplicate parameter names: {}", var);
            std::process::exit(1);
        }
    }

    // Validate that if float range, step required
    if let Some((_, ref min_s, ref max_s)) = param_scan_data {
        let min_is_float = min_s.contains('.') || min_s.contains('e') || min_s.contains('E');
        let max_is_float = max_s.contains('.') || max_s.contains('e') || max_s.contains('E');
        if (min_is_float || max_is_float) && param_step_data.is_none() {
            eprintln!("Error: A step size is required when the range bounds are floating point numbers. The step size can be specified with the '-D/--parameter-step-size <DELTA>' parameter");
            std::process::exit(1);
        }
    }

    // Determine number of benchmark commands including reference for validation
    // But we need to expand parameters to get final count.
    // For validation of --prepare, --conclude, --output counts (must be 1 or N)
    // And command-name validation.

    // Let's compute expanded command list.

    // First, determine shell
    let shell_opt: String = if cli.shell_none {
        "none".to_string()
    } else if let Some(s) = cli.shell {
        s
    } else {
        "default".to_string()
    };

    // Validate shell can be executed? We'll test calibration later.

    // Check commands present
    let mut base_commands: Vec<String> = cli.commands.clone();
    let reference_opt = cli.reference.clone();
    let has_reference = reference_opt.is_some();

    // If no commands, error
    if base_commands.is_empty() {
        eprintln!("error: the following required arguments were not provided:\n  <command>...\n\nUsage: executable [OPTIONS] <command>...\n\nFor more information, try '--help'.");
        std::process::exit(2);
    }

    // Parameter expansion logic
    #[derive(Clone)]
    struct ParamDef {
        var: String,
        values: Vec<String>, // string representation for replacement
        orig_min: Option<String>,
        orig_step: Option<String>,
    }

    let mut param_defs: Vec<ParamDef> = Vec::new();

    if let Some((var,min_s,max_s)) = param_scan_data {
        // parse min, max as f64, step as f64
        let step_s = param_step_data.unwrap_or_else(|| "1".to_string());
        // Store orig strings for formatting first value
        let min_f: f64 = min_s.parse().unwrap_or_else(|_| { eprintln!("Error parsing min"); std::process::exit(1); });
        let max_f: f64 = max_s.parse().unwrap_or_else(|_| { eprintln!("Error parsing max"); std::process::exit(1); });
        let step_f: f64 = step_s.parse().unwrap_or_else(|_| { eprintln!("Error parsing step"); std::process::exit(1); });

        if step_f <= 0.0 {
            eprintln!("Error: step size must be positive");
            std::process::exit(1);
        }

        // Generate sequence
        let mut values_str: Vec<String> = Vec::new();
        // Keep original min string for first value
        // Determine decimal places of step and min for formatting subsequent values
        // We'll attempt to reproduce hyperfine's formatting as best as possible.
        fn decimal_places(s: &str) -> usize {
            if let Some(pos) = s.find('.') {
                s[pos+1..].len()
            } else {
                0
            }
        }
        fn significant_decimal_places(s: &str) -> usize {
            if let Some(pos) = s.find('.') {
                let frac = &s[pos+1..];
                let trimmed = frac.trim_end_matches('0');
                trimmed.len()
            } else {
                0
            }
        }

        let step_dec = decimal_places(&step_s);
        // For subsequent values, we need to decide formatting.
        // We'll use heuristic matching earlier analysis.

        let mut current = min_f;
        let mut idx=0;
        loop {
            // Stop when current > max + epsilon
            if current > max_f + 1e-9 {
                break;
            }
            if idx==0 {
                values_str.push(min_s.clone()); // preserve original
            } else {
                // format current based on step dec and maybe min fractional significant?
                // Heuristic: format with max(step_dec, significant dec of min if current fractional non-zero?)
                // Actually we determined rule: use step_dec, but if current has non-zero fractional that needs more than step_dec, use max.
                // Simpler: determine precision = max(step_dec, significant_decimal_places of min if min has non-zero fractional and step dec ==0? Let's implement earlier derived rule:
                // For subsequent values, precision = max(step_dec, significant_decimal_places_of_min) ??? But that fails for 0.00 case.
                // Let's try to compute current's fractional part and see if it needs more than step_dec.
                // Better: format current with step_dec decimals, then trim? But for 0.5 2.5 step1, step_dec=0, formatting with 0 dec gives "1","2" not "1.5","2.5". So need at least 1 dec for those.
                // So we need to know MIN's fractional part: if MIN is like 0.5, then adding integer steps keeps .5, so need 1 dec.
                // So we could compute fractional part of MIN (significant) and if it's non-zero, we need at least that many decimals.
                // For MIN=0.00 significant=0, step dec=0 => 0 dec.
                // For MIN=0.5 significant=1, step dec=0 => max=1 => 1 dec.
                // For MIN=0.00 significant=0, step dec=1 => max=1 => 1 dec.
                // For MIN=0.00 significant=0, step dec=0.5? Actually step 0.5 has 1 dec, so max=1 => 1 dec.

                // Let's compute needed dec as max(step_dec, min_significant) where min_significant is significant decimal of original MIN? For MIN=0.00 significant 0, step 1 dec 1 => max 1 => gives 0.5,1.0 etc (1 dec) which matches 0.00 1.00 0.5 case: first is 0.00 (original), second 0.5 (1 dec), third 1.0 (1 dec) => matches.

                // For MIN=0.00 scenario with step 1: significant 0, step 0 => max 0 => subsequent 1,2 (0 dec) matches.

                // For MIN=0.5 (significant 1) step 1 (0): max 1 => 1.5,2.5 (1 dec) matches.

                // For MIN=0 (significant 0) step 0.25 (2): max 2 => 0.25,0.50,0.75,1.00 (2 dec) matches.

                // For MIN=0.0 (significant 0) step 0.25 (2): max 2 => 0.25,0.50,0.75,1.00 -> first is 0.0 (original) but subsequent have 2 dec -> observed for that case: 0.0,0.25,0.50,0.75,1.00 matches.

                // For MIN=0.5 (1) step 0.25 (2): max 2 => 0.75,1.00,1.25... observed earlier had 0.75,1.00,1.25... matches.

                // For MIN=0.00 (0) step 0.33 (2): max 2 => 0.33,0.66,0.99 matches.

                // So rule: precision for subsequent values = max(step_dec, significant_dec_of_min) ??? But for MIN=0.00 significant 0, step dec 1 => max 1 => 0.5,1.0 etc (1 dec) matches.

                // For MIN=0 (0) step 2.5 (1): max 1 => 2.5,5.0,7.5,10.0 => matches (1 dec).

                // For MIN=0 (0) step 0.5 (1): max 1 => 0.5,1.0 etc matches.

                // For MIN=0.00 step 0.5: significant 0, step 1 => 1 dec => matches earlier.

                // For MIN=0.0 step 1: significant 0, step 0 => 0 dec => 1,2 matches.

                // For MIN=0.5 step 1: significant 1, step 0 => max 1 => 1.5,2.5 matches.

                // Good! So we have a plausible rule.

                // However what about case where MIN=0.00 (0 significant) step=1 (0) but we want 1,2 not 1.00,2.00 => max 0 => 0 dec => matches.

                // Let's adopt this.

                let min_significant = significant_decimal_places(&min_s);
                let prec = std::cmp::max(step_dec, min_significant);
                let fmt = if prec==0 {
                    format!("{:.0}", current)
                } else {
                    format!("{:.*}", prec, current)
                };
                // But this would format 1.0 as "1" if prec=0, not "1.0". That's correct for prec 0.
                // For prec 1, 1.0 would be "1.0" (good), 5 -> 5.0? With prec 1, format!("{:.1}",5.0) => "5.0" good.
                // For 0.5 with prec 1 => "0.5" good.
                // However floating errors may cause 0.1+0.2 etc.
                values_str.push(fmt);
            }
            current += step_f;
            idx+=1;
            // To avoid infinite loop, limit iterations
            if idx>10000 { break; }
        }

        param_defs.push(ParamDef { var, values: values_str, orig_min: Some(min_s), orig_step: Some(step_s) });
    }

    for list in cli.parameter_list {
        let var = list[0].clone();
        let vals_str = list[1].clone();
        let split: Vec<String> = vals_str.split(',').map(|s| s.trim().to_string()).filter(|s| !s.is_empty()).collect();
        if split.is_empty() {
            eprintln!("Error: parameter list empty for {}", var);
            std::process::exit(1);
        }
        param_defs.push(ParamDef { var, values: split, orig_min: None, orig_step: None });
    }

    // Now expand commands: Cartesian product of param_defs
    // Each param_def has multiple values. The total combinations is product of lengths.
    // For each base command, for each combination, generate expanded command string by replacing {VAR} with value
    // And generate display name logic.

    // First compute all combinations of param values
    #[derive(Clone)]
    struct Combination {
        map: HashMap<String,String>,
    }

    fn generate_combinations(defs: &[ParamDef]) -> Vec<Combination> {
        if defs.is_empty() {
            return vec![Combination{map: HashMap::new()}];
        }
        let mut result = Vec::new();
        let first = &defs[0];
        let rest = &defs[1..];
        let rest_combos = generate_combinations(rest);
        for val in &first.values {
            for combo in &rest_combos {
                let mut map = combo.map.clone();
                map.insert(first.var.clone(), val.clone());
                result.push(Combination{map});
            }
        }
        result
    }

    let combinations = generate_combinations(&param_defs);

    // For each base command, for each combination, produce final command string and parameter map for JSON
    struct ExpandedCommand {
        original: String,
        expanded: String,
        params: HashMap<String,String>,
        // For display name suffix detection: which vars were not found in original command placeholder?
        missing_vars: Vec<String>, // vars that were not replaced because placeholder not present
    }

    let mut expanded_commands: Vec<ExpandedCommand> = Vec::new();
    for base in &base_commands {
        for combo in &combinations {
            let mut exp = base.clone();
            let mut missing = Vec::new();
            for (var,val) in &combo.map {
                let placeholder = format!("{{{}}}", var);
                if exp.contains(&placeholder) {
                    exp = exp.replace(&placeholder, val);
                } else {
                    missing.push(var.clone());
                }
            }
            expanded_commands.push(ExpandedCommand{
                original: base.clone(),
                expanded: exp,
                params: combo.map.clone(),
                missing_vars: missing,
            });
        }
    }

    // Now handle reference expansion similarly? Reference command also should be parameter-expanded? The earlier test with --reference and -P: reference was not expanded? Actually we tested reference with param scan and output included ref plus param values. Let's check: hyperfine -P x 1 2 --reference 'echo ref' 'echo {x}' -> Benchmarks: ref, echo 1, echo 2. So reference is NOT expanded with parameter values (it's independent). That suggests reference command is not parameterized? Or is it expanded but with no placeholder? In our test, reference didn't have placeholder, so would be duplicated if expanded? But we had only one ref benchmark, not 2. So reference is NOT expanded over parameter combinations.           Set the shell to use for executing benchmarked commands. This can be
          the name or the path to the shell executable, or a full command line
          like "bash --norc". It can also be set to "default" to explicitly
          select the default shell on this platform. Finally, this can also be
          set to "none" to disable the shell. In this case, commands will be
          executed directly. They can still have arguments, but more complex
          things like "sleep 0.1; sleep 0.2" are not possible without a shell.
  -N
          An alias for '--shell=none'.
  -i, --ignore-failure[=<MODE>]
          Ignore failures of the benchmarked programs. Without a value or with
          'all-non-zero', all non-zero exit codes are ignored. You can also
          provide a comma-separated list of exit codes to ignore (e.g.,
          --ignore-failure=1,2).
      --style <TYPE>
          Set output style type (default: auto). Set this to 'basic' to disable
          output coloring and interactive elements. Set it to 'full' to enable
          all effects even if no interactive terminal was detected. Set this to
          'nocolor' to keep the interactive output without any colors. Set this
          to 'color' to keep the colors without any interactive output. Set this
          to 'none' to disable all the output of the tool.
      --sort <METHOD>
          Specify the sort order of the speed comparison summary and the
          exported tables for markup formats (Markdown, AsciiDoc, org-mode):
            * 'auto' (default): the speed comparison will be ordered by time and
              the markup tables will be ordered by command (input order).
            * 'command': order benchmarks in the way they were specified
            * 'mean-time': order benchmarks by mean runtime
  -u, --time-unit <UNIT>
          Set the time unit to be used. Possible values: microsecond,
          millisecond, second. If the option is not given, the time unit is
          determined automatically. This option affects the standard output as
          well as all export formats except for CSV and JSON.
      --export-asciidoc <FILE>
          Export the timing summary statistics as an AsciiDoc table to the given
          FILE. The output time unit can be changed using the --time-unit
          option.
      --export-csv <FILE>
          Export the timing summary statistics as CSV to the given FILE. If you
          need the timing results for each individual run, use the JSON export
          format. The output time unit is always seconds.
      --export-json <FILE>
          Export the timing summary statistics and timings of individual runs as
          JSON to the given FILE. The output time unit is always seconds
      --export-markdown <FILE>
          Export the timing summary statistics as a Markdown table to the given
          FILE. The output time unit can be changed using the --time-unit
          option.
      --export-orgmode <FILE>
          Export the timing summary statistics as an Emacs org-mode table to the
          given FILE. The output time unit can be changed using the --time-unit
          option.
      --show-output
          Print the stdout and stderr of the benchmark instead of suppressing
          it. This will increase the time it takes for benchmarks to run, so it
          should only be used for debugging purposes or when trying to benchmark
          output speed.
      --output <WHERE>
          Control where the output of the benchmark is redirected. Note that
          some programs like 'grep' detect when standard output is /dev/null and
          apply certain optimizations. To avoid that, consider using
          '--output=pipe'.
          
          <WHERE> can be:
          
            null:     Redirect output to /dev/null (the default).
          
            pipe:     Feed the output through a pipe before discarding it.
          
            inherit:  Don't redirect the output at all (same as
            '--show-output').
          
            <FILE>:   Write the output to the given file.
          
          This option can be specified once for all commands or multiple times,
          once for each command. Note: If you want to log the output of each and
          every iteration, you can use a shell redirection and the
          '$HYPERFINE_ITERATION' environment variable:
              hyperfine 'my-command > output-${HYPERFINE_ITERATION}.log'
      --input <WHERE>
          Control where the input of the benchmark comes from.
          
          <WHERE> can be:
          
            null:     Read from /dev/null (the default).
          
            <FILE>:   Read the input from the given file.
  -n, --command-name <NAME>
          Give a meaningful name to a command. This can be specified multiple
          times if several commands are benchmarked.
  -h, --help
          Print help
  -V, --version
          Print version
"#;
    println!("{}", help);
}

fn main() {
    let args: Vec<String> = env::args().collect();
    for a in &args[1..] {
        if a=="-h" || a=="--help" {
            print_help();
            std::process::exit(0);
        }
        if a=="-V" || a=="--version" {
            println!("hyperfine 1.20.0");
            std::process::exit(0);
        }
    }

    let cmd = Command::new("hyperfine")
        .version("1.20.0")
        .about("A command-line benchmarking tool.")
        .disable_help_flag(true)
        .disable_version_flag(true)
        .override_usage("executable [OPTIONS] <command>...")
        .arg(Arg::new("warmup").short('w').long("warmup").value_name("NUM"))
        .arg(Arg::new("min-runs").short('m').long("min-runs").value_name("NUM"))
        .arg(Arg::new("max-runs").short('M').long("max-runs").value_name("NUM"))
        .arg(Arg::new("runs").short('r').long("runs").value_name("NUM"))
        .arg(Arg::new("setup").short('s').long("setup").value_name("CMD"))
        .arg(Arg::new("reference").long("reference").value_name("CMD"))
        .arg(Arg::new("reference-name").long("reference-name").value_name("CMD").requires("reference"))
        .arg(Arg::new("prepare").short('p').long("prepare").value_name("CMD").action(ArgAction::Append))
        .arg(Arg::new("conclude").short('C').long("conclude").value_name("CMD").action(ArgAction::Append))
        .arg(Arg::new("cleanup").short('c').long("cleanup").value_name("CMD"))
        .arg(Arg::new("parameter-scan").short('P').long("parameter-scan").value_names(["VAR","MIN","MAX"]).num_args(3))
        .arg(Arg::new("parameter-step-size").short('D').long("parameter-step-size").value_name("DELTA").requires("parameter-scan"))
        .arg(Arg::new("parameter-list").short('L').long("parameter-list").value_names(["VAR","VALUES"]).num_args(2).action(ArgAction::Append))
        .arg(Arg::new("shell").short('S').long("shell").value_name("SHELL"))
        .arg(Arg::new("shell_none").short('N').action(ArgAction::SetTrue).conflicts_with("shell"))
        .arg(Arg::new("ignore-failure").short('i').long("ignore-failure").value_name("MODE").num_args(0..=1).default_missing_value(""))
        .arg(Arg::new("style").long("style").value_name("TYPE").conflicts_with("show-output"))
        .arg(Arg::new("sort").long("sort").value_name("METHOD"))
        .arg(Arg::new("time-unit").short('u').long("time-unit").value_name("UNIT"))
        .arg(Arg::new("export-asciidoc").long("export-asciidoc").value_name("FILE"))
        .arg(Arg::new("export-csv").long("export-csv").value_name("FILE"))
        .arg(Arg::new("export-json").long("export-json").value_name("FILE"))
        .arg(Arg::new("export-markdown").long("export-markdown").value_name("FILE"))
        .arg(Arg::new("export-orgmode").long("export-orgmode").value_name("FILE"))
        .arg(Arg::new("show-output").long("show-output").action(ArgAction::SetTrue).conflicts_with("output"))
        .arg(Arg::new("output").long("output").value_name("WHERE").action(ArgAction::Append))
        .arg(Arg::new("input").long("input").value_name("WHERE"))
        .arg(Arg::new("command-name").short('n').long("command-name").value_name("NAME").action(ArgAction::Append))
        .arg(Arg::new("help").short('h').long("help").action(ArgAction::SetTrue))
        .arg(Arg::new("version").short('V').long("version").action(ArgAction::SetTrue))
        .arg(Arg::new("command").value_name("command").trailing_var_arg(true).allow_hyphen_values(true).num_args(0..));

    let matches = match cmd.try_get_matches() {
        Ok(m) => m,
        Err(e) => {
            e.print().unwrap();
            std::process::exit(e.exit_code());
        }
    };

    if matches.get_flag("help") {
        print_help();
        std::process::exit(0);
    }
    if matches.get_flag("version") {
        println!("hyperfine 1.20.0");
        std::process::exit(0);
    }

    let warmup: Option<u64> = matches.get_one::<String>("warmup").and_then(|s| s.parse().ok());
    let min_runs: Option<u64> = matches.get_one::<String>("min-runs").and_then(|s| s.parse().ok());
    let max_runs: Option<u64> = matches.get_one::<String>("max-runs").and_then(|s| s.parse().ok());
    let runs: Option<u64> = matches.get_one::<String>("runs").and_then(|s| s.parse().ok());
    let setup: Option<String> = matches.get_one::<String>("setup").cloned();
    let reference: Option<String> = matches.get_one::<String>("reference").cloned();
    let reference_name: Option<String> = matches.get_one::<String>("reference-name").cloned();
    let prepare: Vec<String> = matches.get_many::<String>("prepare").map(|v| v.cloned().collect()).unwrap_or_default();
    let conclude: Vec<String> = matches.get_many::<String>("conclude").map(|v| v.cloned().collect()).unwrap_or_default();
    let cleanup: Option<String> = matches.get_one::<String>("cleanup").cloned();
    let parameter_scan: Option<Vec<String>> = matches.get_many::<String>("parameter-scan").map(|v| v.cloned().collect());
    let parameter_step_size: Option<String> = matches.get_one::<String>("parameter-step-size").cloned();

    let mut param_list_manual: Vec<Vec<String>> = Vec::new();
    {
        let raw: Vec<String> = env::args().collect();
        let mut i=1;
        while i<raw.len() {
            let a = &raw[i];
            if a=="-L" || a=="--parameter-list" {
                if i+2 < raw.len() {
                    let var = raw[i+1].clone();
                    let vals = raw[i+2].clone();
                    param_list_manual.push(vec![var, vals]);
                    i+=3;
                    continue;
                }
            }
            i+=1;
        }
    }
    let parameter_list = param_list_manual;

    let shell: Option<String> = matches.get_one::<String>("shell").cloned();
    let shell_none = matches.get_flag("shell_none");
    let ignore_failure: Option<String> = matches.get_one::<String>("ignore-failure").cloned();
    let style: Option<String> = matches.get_one::<String>("style").cloned();
    let sort: Option<String> = matches.get_one::<String>("sort").cloned();
    let time_unit: Option<String> = matches.get_one::<String>("time-unit").cloned();
    let export_asciidoc: Option<String> = matches.get_one::<String>("export-asciidoc").cloned();
    let export_csv: Option<String> = matches.get_one::<String>("export-csv").cloned();
    let export_json: Option<String> = matches.get_one::<String>("export-json").cloned();
    let export_markdown: Option<String> = matches.get_one::<String>("export-markdown").cloned();
    let export_orgmode: Option<String> = matches.get_one::<String>("export-orgmode").cloned();
    let show_output = matches.get_flag("show-output");
    let output: Vec<String> = matches.get_many::<String>("output").map(|v| v.cloned().collect()).unwrap_or_default();
    let input: Option<String> = matches.get_one::<String>("input").cloned();
    let command_name: Vec<String> = matches.get_many::<String>("command-name").map(|v| v.cloned().collect()).unwrap_or_default();
    let commands: Vec<String> = matches.get_many::<String>("command").map(|v| v.cloned().collect()).unwrap_or_default();

    // Validation
    if let Some(ref tu) = time_unit {
        match tu.as_str() {
            "microsecond"|"millisecond"|"second" => {},
            _ => {
                eprintln!("error: invalid value '{}' for '--time-unit <UNIT>'\n  [possible values: microsecond, millisecond, second]\n\n  tip: a similar value exists: 'second'\n\nFor more information, try '--help'.", tu);
                std::process::exit(2);
            }
        }
    }
    if let Some(ref s) = sort {
        match s.as_str() {
            "auto"|"command"|"mean-time" => {},
            _ => {
                eprintln!("error: invalid value '{}' for '--sort <METHOD>'\n  [possible values: auto, command, mean-time]\n\nFor more information, try '--help'.", s);
                std::process::exit(2);
            }
        }
    }
    if let Some(ref st) = style {
        match st.as_str() {
            "auto"|"basic"|"full"|"nocolor"|"color"|"none" => {},
            _ => {
                eprintln!("error: invalid value '{}' for '--style <TYPE>'\n  [possible values: auto, basic, full, nocolor, color, none]\n\nFor more information, try '--help'.", st);
                std::process::exit(2);
            }
        }
    }

    if parameter_scan.is_some() && !parameter_list.is_empty() {
        eprintln!("error: the argument '--parameter-list <VAR> <VALUES>' cannot be used with '--parameter-scan <VAR> <MIN> <MAX>'\n\nUsage: executable --parameter-list <VAR> <VALUES> --runs <NUM> <command>...\n\nFor more information, try '--help'.");
        std::process::exit(2);
    }

    let mut param_names_set = HashSet::new();
    for pair in &parameter_list {
        let name = &pair[0];
        if param_names_set.contains(name) {
            eprintln!("Error: Duplicate parameter names: {}", name);
            std::process::exit(1);
        }
        param_names_set.insert(name.clone());
    }
    if let Some(v) = &parameter_scan {
        let var = &v[0];
        if param_names_set.contains(var) {
            eprintln!("Error: Duplicate parameter names: {}", var);
            std::process::exit(1);
        }
    }

    if let Some(v) = &parameter_scan {
        let min_s = &v[1];
        let max_s = &v[2];
        let min_is_float = min_s.contains('.') || min_s.contains('e') || min_s.contains('E');
        let max_is_float = max_s.contains('.') || max_s.contains('e') || max_s.contains('E');
        if (min_is_float || max_is_float) && parameter_step_size.is_none() {
            eprintln!("Error: A step size is required when the range bounds are floating point numbers. The step size can be specified with the '-D/--parameter-step-size <DELTA>' parameter");
            std::process::exit(1);
        }
    }

    let shell_opt_str: String = if shell_none { "none".to_string() } else if let Some(s) = shell.clone() { s } else { "default".to_string() };
    let base_commands = commands;
    if base_commands.is_empty() {
        eprintln!("error: the following required arguments were not provided:\n  <command>...\n\nUsage: executable [OPTIONS] <command>...\n\nFor more information, try '--help'.");
        std::process::exit(2);
    }

    #[derive(Clone)]
    struct ParamDef { var: String, values: Vec<String> }

    let mut param_defs: Vec<ParamDef> = Vec::new();

    if let Some(v) = &parameter_scan {
        let var = v[0].clone();
        let min_s = v[1].clone();
        let max_s = v[2].clone();
        let step_s = parameter_step_size.clone().unwrap_or_else(|| "1".to_string());
        let min_f: f64 = min_s.parse().unwrap_or_else(|_| { eprintln!("Error parsing min"); std::process::exit(1); });
        let max_f: f64 = max_s.parse().unwrap_or_else(|_| { eprintln!("Error parsing max"); std::process::exit(1); });
        let step_f: f64 = step_s.parse().unwrap_or_else(|_| { eprintln!("Error parsing step"); std::process::exit(1); });
        if step_f <= 0.0 { eprintln!("Error: step size must be positive"); std::process::exit(1); }
        fn decimal_places(s: &str) -> usize { if let Some(pos) = s.find('.') { s[pos+1..].len() } else { 0 } }
        fn significant_decimal_places(s: &str) -> usize { if let Some(pos) = s.find('.') { let frac = &s[pos+1..]; let trimmed = frac.trim_end_matches('0'); trimmed.len() } else { 0 } }
        let step_dec = decimal_places(&step_s);
        let min_sig = significant_decimal_places(&min_s);
        let mut values_str = Vec::new();
        let mut current = min_f;
        let mut idx = 0;
        loop {
            if current > max_f + 1e-9 { break; }
            if idx==0 {
                values_str.push(min_s.clone());
            } else {
                let prec = std::cmp::max(step_dec, min_sig);
                let fmt = if prec==0 { format!("{:.0}", current) } else { format!("{:.*}", prec, current) };
                values_str.push(fmt);
            }
            current += step_f;
            idx+=1;
            if idx>10000 { break; }
        }
        param_defs.push(ParamDef{ var, values: values_str });
    }

    for pair in &parameter_list {
        let var = pair[0].clone();
        let vals_str = pair[1].clone();
        let split: Vec<String> = vals_str.split(',').map(|s| s.trim().to_string()).filter(|s| !s.is_empty()).collect();
        if split.is_empty() { eprintln!("Error: parameter list empty for {}", var); std::process::exit(1); }
        param_defs.push(ParamDef{ var, values: split });
    }

    #[derive(Clone)]
    struct Combination { map: HashMap<String,String> }

    fn generate_combinations(defs: &[ParamDef]) -> Vec<Combination> {
        if defs.is_empty() { return vec![Combination{map: HashMap::new()}]; }
        let mut result = Vec::new();
        let first = &defs[0];
        let rest = &defs[1..];
        let rest_combos = generate_combinations(rest);
        for val in &first.values {
            for combo in &rest_combos {
                let mut map = combo.map.clone();
                map.insert(first.var.clone(), val.clone());
                result.push(Combination{map});
            }
        }
        result
    }

    let combinations = generate_combinations(&param_defs);

    struct ExpandedCommand {
        original: String,
        expanded: String,
        params: HashMap<String,String>,
        missing_vars: Vec<String>,
    }

    let mut expanded_commands: Vec<ExpandedCommand> = Vec::new();
    for base in &base_commands {
        for combo in &combinations {
            let mut exp = base.clone();
            let mut missing = Vec::new();
            for (var,val) in &combo.map {
                let placeholder = format!("{{{}}}", var);
                if exp.contains(&placeholder) {
                    exp = exp.replace(&placeholder, val);
                } else {
                    missing.push(var.clone());
                }
            }
            missing.sort();
            expanded_commands.push(ExpandedCommand{ original: base.clone(), expanded: exp, params: combo.map.clone(), missing_vars: missing });
        }
    }

    let has_reference = reference.is_some();
    let num_benchmarks_total = expanded_commands.len() + if has_reference {1} else {0};

    fn validate_count(name: &str, vec: &[String], n: usize) {
        if vec.is_empty() { return; }
        if vec.len()!=1 && vec.len()!=n {
            eprintln!("Error: The '{}' option has to be provided just once or N times, where N={} is the number of benchmark commands (including a potential reference).", name, n);
            std::process::exit(1);
        }
    }

    validate_count("--prepare", &prepare, num_benchmarks_total);
    validate_count("--conclude", &conclude, num_benchmarks_total);
    validate_count("--output", &output, num_benchmarks_total);

    if !command_name.is_empty() {
        if param_defs.is_empty() {
            let n = base_commands.len();
            if command_name.len() > n {
                eprintln!("Error: Too many --command-name options: Expected {} at most", n);
                std::process::exit(1);
            }
        } else {
            let n = expanded_commands.len();
            let c = command_name.len();
            if c!=0 && c!=1 && c!=n {
                eprintln!("Error: '--command-name' has been specified {} times. It has to appear exactly once, or exactly {} times (number of benchmarks)", c, n);
                std::process::exit(1);
            }
        }
    }

    for out in &output {
        if out=="null" || out=="pipe" || out=="inherit" { continue; }
        if out.contains('/') { continue; }
        else {
            eprintln!("Error: Unknown output policy '{}'. Use './{}' to output to a file named '{}'.", out, out, out);
            std::process::exit(1);
        }
    }

    if let Some(ref inp) = input {
        if inp!="null" {
            let p = Path::new(inp);
            if !p.exists() {
                eprintln!("Error: The file '{}' specified as '--input' does not exist", inp);
                std::process::exit(1);
            }
        }
    }

    let style_str = style.unwrap_or_else(|| "auto".to_string());
    let style = style_str.as_str();
    let sort_method = sort.unwrap_or_else(|| "auto".to_string());
    let time_unit_opt = time_unit.clone();
    let shell_default_path = "/bin/sh".to_string();
    let effective_shell: Option<Vec<String>> = if shell_opt_str=="none" {
        None
    } else if shell_opt_str=="default" {
        Some(vec![shell_default_path.clone()])
    } else {
        fn split_shell(s: &str) -> Vec<String> {
            let mut res = Vec::new();
            let mut cur = String::new();
            let mut in_single = false;
            let mut in_double = false;
            let mut escape = false;
            for c in s.chars() {
                if escape { cur.push(c); escape=false; continue; }
                if c=='\\' && !in_single { escape=true; continue; }
                if c=='\'' && !in_double { in_single=!in_single; continue; }
                if c=='"' && !in_single { in_double=!in_double; continue; }
                if c.is_whitespace() && !in_single && !in_double {
                    if !cur.is_empty() { res.push(cur.clone()); cur.clear(); }
                } else { cur.push(c); }
            }
            if !cur.is_empty() { res.push(cur); }
            res
        }
        let parts = split_shell(&shell_opt_str);
        if parts.is_empty() { Some(vec![shell_default_path.clone()]) } else { Some(parts) }
    };

    let mut shell_overhead = Duration::from_secs_f64(0.0);
    if let Some(ref shell_parts) = effective_shell {
        let shell_exe = &shell_parts[0];
        let shell_args = &shell_parts[1..];
        let mut times = Vec::new();
        for _ in 0..10 {
            let start = Instant::now();
            let mut cmd = ProcCommand::new(shell_exe);
            for a in shell_args { cmd.arg(a); }
            cmd.arg("-c"); cmd.arg("");
            cmd.stdout(Stdio::null()); cmd.stderr(Stdio::null()); cmd.stdin(Stdio::null());
            match cmd.status() {
                Ok(st) => {
                    if !st.success() {
                        eprintln!("Error: Could not measure shell execution time. Make sure you can run '{} -c \"\"'.", shell_opt_str);
                        std::process::exit(1);
                    }
                    times.push(start.elapsed());
                },
                Err(_) => {
                    eprintln!("Error: Could not measure shell execution time. Make sure you can run '{} -c \"\"'.", shell_opt_str);
                    std::process::exit(1);
                }
            }
        }
        let sum: Duration = times.iter().sum();
        shell_overhead = sum / (times.len() as u32);
    }

    #[derive(Clone)]
    enum IgnoreMode { All, Codes(HashSet<i32>) }
    let ignore_mode: Option<IgnoreMode> = if let Some(ref s) = ignore_failure {
        if s.is_empty() || s=="all-non-zero" {
            Some(IgnoreMode::All)
        } else {
            let mut set = HashSet::new();
            for part in s.split(',') {
                let p = part.trim();
                if p.is_empty() { continue; }
                if let Ok(code) = p.parse::<i32>() { set.insert(code); }
            }
            Some(IgnoreMode::Codes(set))
        }
    } else { None };

    fn execute_command(
        command_str: &str,
        shell_opt: &Option<Vec<String>>,
        iteration: usize,
        input_opt: &Option<String>,
        output_opt: &str,
        show_output: bool,
        shell_overhead: Duration,
    ) -> Result<(Duration, Duration, Duration, i32, u64), String> {
        fn split_cmd(s: &str) -> Vec<String> {
            let mut res = Vec::new();
            let mut cur = String::new();
            let mut in_single = false;
            let mut in_double = false;
            let mut escape = false;
            for c in s.chars() {
                if escape { cur.push(c); escape=false; continue; }
                if c=='\\' && !in_single { escape=true; continue; }
                if c=='\'' && !in_double { in_single=!in_single; continue; }
                if c=='"' && !in_single { in_double=!in_double; continue; }
                if c.is_whitespace() && !in_single && !in_double {
                    if !cur.is_empty() { res.push(cur.clone()); cur.clear(); }
                } else { cur.push(c); }
            }
            if !cur.is_empty() { res.push(cur); }
            res
        }

        let start = Instant::now();

        let mut proc = if let Some(shell_parts) = shell_opt {
            let shell_exe = &shell_parts[0];
            let shell_args = &shell_parts[1..];
            let mut cmd = ProcCommand::new(shell_exe);
            for a in shell_args { cmd.arg(a); }
            cmd.arg("-c"); cmd.arg(command_str);
            cmd.env("HYPERFINE_ITERATION", iteration.to_string());
            match input_opt {
                None => { cmd.stdin(Stdio::null()); },
                Some(s) if s=="null" => { cmd.stdin(Stdio::null()); },
                Some(file) => {
                    match File::open(file) {
                        Ok(f) => { cmd.stdin(Stdio::from(f)); },
                        Err(_) => { cmd.stdin(Stdio::null()); },
                    }
                }
            }
            if show_output {
                cmd.stdout(Stdio::inherit()); cmd.stderr(Stdio::inherit());
            } else {
                match output_opt {
                    "null" => { cmd.stdout(Stdio::null()); cmd.stderr(Stdio::null()); },
                    "pipe" => { cmd.stdout(Stdio::piped()); cmd.stderr(Stdio::piped()); },
                    "inherit" => { cmd.stdout(Stdio::inherit()); cmd.stderr(Stdio::inherit()); },
                    _ => {
                        let path = if output_opt.starts_with("./") { &output_opt[2..] } else { output_opt };
                        match OpenOptions::new().create(true).write(true).truncate(true).open(path) {
                            Ok(f) => {
                                let f2 = f.try_clone().unwrap();
                                cmd.stdout(Stdio::from(f));
                                cmd.stderr(Stdio::from(f2));
                            },
                            Err(_) => { cmd.stdout(Stdio::null()); cmd.stderr(Stdio::null()); }
                        }
                    }
                }
            }
            cmd.spawn().map_err(|e| e.to_string())?
        } else {
            let parts = split_cmd(command_str);
            if parts.is_empty() {
                let mut cmd = ProcCommand::new("true");
                cmd.env("HYPERFINE_ITERATION", iteration.to_string());
                match input_opt {
                    None => { cmd.stdin(Stdio::null()); },
                    Some(s) if s=="null" => { cmd.stdin(Stdio::null()); },
                    Some(file) => {
                        match File::open(file) {
                            Ok(f) => { cmd.stdin(Stdio::from(f)); },

                        }

                } else {
                    match output_opt {
                        "null" => { cmd.stdout(Stdio::null()); cmd.stderr(Stdio::null()); },
                        "pipe" => { cmd.stdout(Stdio::piped()); cmd.stderr(Stdio::piped()); },
                        "inherit" => { cmd.stdout(Stdio::inherit()); cmd.stderr(Stdio::inherit()); },
                        _ => {
                            let path = if output_opt.starts_with("./") { &output_opt[2..] } else { output_opt };
                            match OpenOptions::new().create(true).write(true).truncate(true).open(path) {
                                Ok(f) => {
                                    let f2 = f.try_clone().unwrap();
                                    cmd.stdout(Stdio::from(f));
                                    cmd.stderr(Stdio::from(f2));
                                },
                                Err(_) => { cmd.stdout(Stdio::null()); cmd.stderr(Stdio::null()); }
                            }
                        }
                    }
                }
                cmd.spawn().map_err(|e| e.to_string())?
            } else {
                let exe = parts[0].clone();
                let args = parts[1..].to_vec();
                let mut cmd = ProcCommand::new(&exe);
                cmd.args(&args);
                cmd.env("HYPERFINE_ITERATION", iteration.to_string());
                match input_opt {
                    None => { cmd.stdin(Stdio::null()); },
                    Some(s) if s=="null" => { cmd.stdin(Stdio::null()); },
                    Some(file) => {
                        match File::open(file) {
                            Ok(f) => { cmd.stdin(Stdio::from(f)); },
                            Err(_) => { cmd.stdin(Stdio::null()); },
                        }
                    }
                }
                if show_output {
                    cmd.stdout(Stdio::inherit()); cmd.stderr(Stdio::inherit());
                } else {
                    match output_opt {
                        "null" => { cmd.stdout(Stdio::null()); cmd.stderr(Stdio::null()); },
                        "pipe" => { cmd.stdout(Stdio::piped()); cmd.stderr(Stdio::piped()); },
                        "inherit" => { cmd.stdout(Stdio::inherit()); cmd.stderr(Stdio::inherit()); },
                        _ => {
                            let path = if output_opt.starts_with("./") { &output_opt[2..] } else { output_opt };
                            match OpenOptions::new().create(true).write(true).truncate(true).open(path) {
                                Ok(f) => {
                                    let f2 = f.try_clone().unwrap();
                                    cmd.stdout(Stdio::from(f));
                                    cmd.stderr(Stdio::from(f2));
                                },
                                Err(_) => { cmd.stdout(Stdio::null()); cmd.stderr(Stdio::null()); }
                            }
                        }
                    }
                }
                match cmd.spawn() {
                    Ok(p) => p,
                    Err(_) => {
                        let elapsed = start.elapsed();
                        let adjusted = if elapsed > shell_overhead { elapsed - shell_overhead } else { Duration::from_secs_f64(0.0) };
                        return Ok((adjusted, Duration::from_secs_f64(0.0), Duration::from_secs_f64(0.0), 127, 0));
                    }
                }
            }
        };

        let pid = proc.id() as i32;
        let mut status: i32 = 0;
        let mut rusage = unsafe { std::mem::zeroed::<libc::rusage>() };
        let res = unsafe { libc::wait4(pid, &mut status as *mut i32, 0, &mut rusage as *mut libc::rusage) };
        let real_elapsed = start.elapsed();

        if res < 0 {
            let _ = proc.wait();
            let adjusted = if real_elapsed > shell_overhead { real_elapsed - shell_overhead } else { Duration::from_secs_f64(0.0) };
            return Ok((adjusted, Duration::from_secs_f64(0.0), Duration::from_secs_f64(0.0), 127, 0));
        }

        let exit_code = if libc::WIFEXITED(status) { libc::WEXITSTATUS(status) } else if libc::WIFSIGNALED(status) { 128 + libc::WTERMSIG(status) } else { 127 };
        let user = Duration::new(rusage.ru_utime.tv_sec as u64, (rusage.ru_utime.tv_usec as u32)*1000);
        let system = Duration::new(rusage.ru_stime.tv_sec as u64, (rusage.ru_stime.tv_usec as u32)*1000);
        let mem_bytes = (rusage.ru_maxrss as u64) * 1024;

        let adjusted_real = if shell_opt.is_some() {
            if real_elapsed > shell_overhead { real_elapsed - shell_overhead } else { Duration::from_secs_f64(0.0) }
        } else { real_elapsed };

        Ok((adjusted_real, user, system, exit_code, mem_bytes))
    }

    fn run_aux_command(cmd_str: &str, shell_opt: &Option<Vec<String>>, iteration: Option<usize>, show_output: bool) -> std::process::ExitStatus {
        let shell_to_use = if let Some(sp) = shell_opt { sp.clone() } else { vec!["/bin/sh".to_string()] };
        let shell_exe = &shell_to_use[0];
        let shell_args = &shell_to_use[1..];
        let mut proc = ProcCommand::new(shell_exe);
        for a in shell_args { proc.arg(a); }
        proc.arg("-c"); proc.arg(cmd_str);
        if let Some(it) = iteration { proc.env("HYPERFINE_ITERATION", it.to_string()); }
        if show_output {
            proc.stdout(Stdio::inherit()); proc.stderr(Stdio::inherit()); proc.stdin(Stdio::null());
        } else {
            proc.stdout(Stdio::null()); proc.stderr(Stdio::null()); proc.stdin(Stdio::null());
        }
        proc.status().unwrap_or_else(|_| ProcCommand::new("false").status().unwrap())
    }

    fn build_suffix(missing: &[String], params: &HashMap<String,String>) -> String {
        if missing.is_empty() { return "".to_string(); }
        let mut parts = Vec::new();
        for var in missing {
            if let Some(val) = params.get(var) { parts.push(format!("{} = {}", var, val)); }
        }
        if parts.is_empty() { "".to_string() } else { format!(" ({})", parts.join(", ")) }
    }

                        let suffix = build_suffix(&exp_cmd.missing_vars, &exp_cmd.params);
                        if suffix.is_empty() { exp_cmd.expanded.clone() } else { format!("{}{}", exp_cmd.original, suffix) }
                    } else if idx < command_name.len() {
                        command_name[idx].clone()
                    } else {
                        let suffix = build_suffix(&exp_cmd.missing_vars, &exp_cmd.params);
                        if suffix.is_empty() { exp_cmd.expanded.clone() } else { format!("{}{}", exp_cmd.original, suffix) }
                    }
                }
            } else {

            } else {

    fn compute_stats(times: &[f64], user_times: &[f64], system_times: &[f64]) -> (f64, Option<f64>, f64, f64, f64, f64, f64) {
        let n = times.len() as f64;
        let sum: f64 = times.iter().sum();
        let mean = sum / n;
        let stddev = if times.len()<=1 { None } else { let var: f64 = times.iter().map(|&x| (x-mean)*(x-mean)).sum::<f64>() / (n-1.0); Some(var.sqrt()) };
        let mut sorted = times.to_vec(); sorted.sort_by(|a,b| a.partial_cmp(b).unwrap());
        let median = if sorted.len()%2==1 { sorted[sorted.len()/2] } else { (sorted[sorted.len()/2 -1] + sorted[sorted.len()/2])/2.0 };
        let user_sum: f64 = user_times.iter().sum(); let user_mean = user_sum / n;
        let sys_sum: f64 = system_times.iter().sum(); let sys_mean = sys_sum / n;
        let min = sorted[0]; let max = sorted[sorted.len()-1];
        (mean, stddev, median, user_mean, sys_mean, min, max)
    }

    fn choose_time_unit_auto(results: &[(BenchSpec, RunData)]) -> String {

            if mean < min_mean { min_mean = mean; }

    }

    fn fmt_time(secs: f64, unit: &str) -> String {
        match unit {
            "microsecond" => format!("{:.1} µs", secs*1_000_000.0),
            "millisecond" => format!("{:.1} ms", secs*1000.0),
            "second" => format!("{:.3} s", secs),
            _ => format!("{:.3} s", secs),
